title: Pareus will not deny God could create man without original righteousness, only that he could make man whole without wholeness
source_text: XXXVI. Pareus tamen asserere non audet, non potuisse naturam humanam absque Originali justitia creari. Nec dicimus, inquit, naturam humanam non potuisse a Deo sine Originali justitia creari. Nos enim terminum divinae ponemus potentiae? saltem dicimus Deum, cum hominem integrum conderet, non potuisse seipsum negare; hominem integrum sine integritate condere. In libr. 1. Bellarm. de Grat. Primi hominis cap. 6. Responsione ad rationem quartam.
pass_a_gloss: Pareus however does not dare to assert that human nature could not have been created without Original justice. Nor do we say, he says, that human nature could not have been created by God without Original justice. For shall we set a limit to divine power? at least we say that God, when he founded integral man, could not deny himself; found integral man without integrity. In book 1. of Bellarm. on the Grace of the First man chap. 6. In the Response to the fourth reason.
pass_b_english: Pareus, however, does not venture to assert that human nature could not have been created without original righteousness. "We do not say," he writes, "that God could not have created human nature without original righteousness. Are we to put a boundary to God's power? What we do say is that when God made man whole, he could not deny himself by making a whole man without wholeness." (On Bellarmine, On the Grace of the First Man, book 1, chapter 6, reply to the fourth argument.)

choices.why: Pareus' wordplay on integer/integritas is kept with 'whole/wholeness'.
